what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Cloudflare runs agents and controls them; its own Agent Access Model leaves room for a signed record of each agent's mandate.
sections.para: From Cloudflare's docs and blog: the Agents SDK, sandboxes, AI Gateway and remote MCP on one side; Access for MCP, WriteGuard, DLP and Web Bot Auth on the other. Controls exist at every layer but default open. Cloudflare's own posts say a scope only says what an agent was allowed to do, not who answers when it gets it wrong. An Agent Behaviour Policy is that record.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Two roles, controls at every layer, open defaults, Cloudflare naming the gap, the policy as the record.
sections.para: Six points; nothing run on Cloudflare yet.

sections.label: Two roles in one account
sections.line: Where agents run, and where they are controlled, often in one account.
sections.para: Agents SDK, Workflows, Sandbox, Browser Run, AI Gateway, OAuth for MCP; Access, the AI security report, DLP, AI Security for Apps, Web Bot Auth.

sections.label: The controls, and what they leave open
sections.line: Seven controls as barriers, each with its gap.
sections.para: Portal tools on by default, scopes advertised not enforced, approvals chosen by the developer, caps on how much not what, bindings without a why, inspection of routed traffic only, identity not mandate.

sections.label: Joe's agent
sections.line: Joe's agent closes thousands of tickets with Joe's permissions.
sections.para: WriteGuard adds client context and risk tiers, but the agent's reach is its human's; only the policy writes down its narrower job.

sections.label: Cloudflare's own case for a mandate
sections.line: Cloudflare's Agent Access Model and trusted-delegation post make the case for a mandate.
sections.para: Declared task scope, default deny, and someone who answers: the mandate, barriers and sign-off of a policy.

sections.label: Read, set, gate, attest
sections.line: Read, set, gate, attest: Cloudflare has pieces at every layer.
sections.para: The missing piece is the signed mandate the logs are checked against.

sections.label: What RiskMandate could offer Cloudflare users
sections.line: A policy per agent read from real configuration, templates, a check of open defaults, a gate from the policy.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not run on Cloudflare; status as each page states; Joe is Cloudflare's example, the mandate ours.
sections.para: No relationship beyond being a customer.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Cloudflare docs and three blog posts, riskmandate.ai and earlier articles.
